Package com.nexuslink.ui.files

Class SameSideMove

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.ui.files.SameSideMove
public final class SameSideMove extends Object
Plans a same-side move — dragging entries into a folder on the very same FileSystem — as a set of FileSystem.rename(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) operations rather than a copy-and-delete. Moving a file inside one server (or one local disk) is just a rename of its path, so there is no reason to stream the bytes down and back up; this decides which renames are legal and what each destination path is, leaving the actual rename I/O and collision handling to the caller. Kept JavaFX-free and unit-testable, mirroring SyncPlanner and DuplicateName.

  • Method Details

    • plan

      public static List<SameSideMove.Move> plan(List<FileItem> items, String destDir, FileSystem fs)
      The legal renames for dropping items into destDir on fs. An entry is dropped from the plan when moving it would be a no-op or nonsensical:
      • the synthetic ".." row;
      • an entry already directly inside destDir (its parent is destDir) — nothing to do;
      • a directory being dropped into itself or into its own subtree — which would detach it from the tree. This is detected via FileSystem.parent(java.lang.String) so it respects the file system's own path semantics rather than guessing at a separator.
      Each surviving entry's destination is FileSystem.join(java.lang.String, java.lang.String)(destDir, name). Collisions with an existing name in destDir are not resolved here (the planner does no I/O); the caller checks FileSystem.exists(java.lang.String, java.lang.String) at execution time.
